clue.text: Crime seen cycling round — system for detection

indicators.note: the letters of the crime's name rotate, the front pair going round to the back

parts.note: arson, the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A crime is spotted going round in circles, flagged by some detection system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling round' moves AR from the front of ARSON to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo-ranging equipment used by ships and submarines to detect objects under water.

clue.text: Tristram's drink

definitions.meaning: Tristram's surname, from Laurence Sterne's novel about a gentleman of that name
a mixed drink of beer and lemonade or ginger beer

explanation.walkthrough: Tristram Shandy is the hero of Laurence Sterne's 18th-century comic novel; the drink is beer topped up with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of Sterne's fictional hero, and also the British name for beer mixed with lemonade.

clue.text: Steals from cop, the ultimate in foolishness

parts.note: to cop is to catch or arrest, as is to nick in British slang

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter, here of foolishness

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly steals from a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a noun for a police officer but is the verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang verb for pilfering, as in someone who pinches a wallet.

clue.text: Time running out, murderous man afflicted with lust founders

indicators.note: time leaving the mix means its letter is taken away from the pool
afflicted suggests the letters are disordered, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A murderous man, tormented by lust, finds his time running out.
explanation.walkthrough: Anagram MURDEROUS MAN plus LUST, then remove T ('Time running out'). The twins of legend founded Rome, and Romulus did kill Remus, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary twin brothers credited with establishing the city of Rome.

clue.text: Tennis player gets championship, one departing in big car

indicators.note: in signals the shortened title goes inside the big car

parts.note: a limo, a long luxury car

indicators.note: one leaving signals that its letter is dropped from the word for championship

parts.note: a title, what a champion holds
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tennis star wins a title and is driven off in a limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departing' drops 'one' from the title, and 'in' puts what is left inside the car. Little Mo was Maureen Connolly, the American tennis champion of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname of Maureen Connolly, who won the tennis Grand Slam in 1953.

clue.text: Left with associate, joke and loiter aimlessly

parts.note: an ally is a partner or associate
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Abandoned with a friend, someone jokes and hangs about with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal, chiefly American verb for dawdling or idling time away.

clue.text: False arrest with copper finally getting out weapon

indicators.note: false suggests the word arrest is not genuine and so is rearranged
getting out means that letter leaves the scrambled word
finally picks the last letter of copper

explanation.surface: A wrongful arrest, and a police officer finally escapes with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ARREST and remove one R, the last letter of 'copper'. 'Copper' looks like a police officer but only gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand-name stun gun firing darts that deliver an electric shock.

clue.text: The prime elements of all these annoying newspaper items

definitions.text: The prime elements of all these annoying
definitions.meaning: the opening letters of all, these and annoying are a, the and an, the three articles of English
editorials, the opinion pieces a paper prints

explanation.walkthrough: A, THE and AN start 'all', 'these' and 'annoying', so they are articles leading those words. The clue's own first word, 'The', is one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials expressing a newspaper's own view; also articles sitting at the front of words.

clue.text: Underground folk protecting bad fashion-designers?

indicators.note: protecting signals one word wrapped around the other

parts.note: miners work underground
ill means bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: Pit workers shield some poor fashion designers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that hat-makers are only one kind of fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Makers of hats, so designers of one part of what people wear.

clue.text: That can be done when shambolic place is reorganised

indicators.note: reorganised means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a chaotic place sorted out is quite feasible.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective meaning achievable or feasible, something capable of being carried out.

clue.text: Girl turned out for show

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, a girl's name
splay describes feet or limbs turned outwards

explanation.surface: A girl turned up for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'attended', but it means splayed, angled outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to exhibit or put on view.

clue.text: Queen unwell and complaining

parts.note: R, for Regina, Latin for queen
ailing means sick or unwell

explanation.surface: The Queen is sick and grumbling about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing at something is protesting or complaining bitterly about it.

clue.text: Building a terminal? This will be part of it

definitions.text: Building a terminal? This will be part of it

indicators.note: being part of the phrase before it means the letters sit inside those words

explanation.surface: Constructing an airport terminal, this will be one component.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Building', 'a' and the start of 'terminal'; the whole clue also defines, since an airport terminal has departure points.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbered departure point where passengers board, part of any airport terminal.

clue.text: Some French fellow, a little beast

parts.note: des is French for some
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Some Frenchman is a little animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small aquatic insect-eating mammal related to moles, found in Russia and the Pyrenees.

clue.text: Ultimately that suet diet is seen to be very poor

indicators.note: the letters are seen in another form, so they are rearranged
ultimately picks the final letter of that

explanation.surface: In the end, a diet of suet looks like it belongs to someone penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the basic necessities of life; utterly impoverished.

clue.text: Old king and elder maybe back to protect our country

indicators.note: to protect means surrounding the country's letters
back signals the word for tree is read backwards

parts.note: the elder is a kind of tree
GB, Great Britain, home of this British puzzle

explanation.surface: An old king and an elder perhaps return to defend Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the tree round, and 'to protect' wraps it around the country. 'elder' looks like an older person but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninth-century King of Wessex, often called the first ruler of all England.

clue.text: One sort of hint or another that's left hidden

indicators.note: hidden means the abbreviation is tucked inside the other hint

parts.note: another sort of hint is a cue

explanation.surface: Two kinds of hint, one of which has been concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points to a second word for a hint, CUE, with L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer towards a solution, of the kind a crossword or a detective story supplies.

clue.text: Condition of youngster being looked after, daughter at sea in battle?

definitions.text: Condition of youngster being looked after

indicators.note: in signals the daughter's letter goes inside the vessel

parts.note: battle with the question mark hints at battleship, a warship, which goes to sea

explanation.surface: A daughter at sea during a battle is being cared for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea in battle?' leads to a battleship, a WARSHIP, with D inside. 'at sea' looks like an anagram signal but it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardianship, the legal state of a minor placed in someone's care.

clue.text: See Carol trailing in game

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: Look, Carol is behind in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind on the scoreboard during a match.

clue.text: Stars of game hugged by Greek characters

indicators.note: hugged by means held inside the other word

parts.note: taus, more than one of the Greek letter tau
RU, rugby union

explanation.surface: Stars of a match are embraced by Greek people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek characters' looks like people but means letters of the alphabet; 'Stars' looks like celebrities but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bull, a constellation and sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Bodily region said to be a barrier

indicators.note: said signals the word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: the groin, where the thigh meets the abdomen

explanation.surface: A part of the body is said to be an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall built out from a beach to check erosion of sand and shingle.

clue.text: Saw magpie flying across river

indicators.note: across means the scrambled bird spans the river's letter
flying suggests the bird's letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone saw a magpie flying over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' scrambles MAGPIE, and 'across' puts it around R. 'Saw' looks like a verb but is a noun, a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying; a witty, pithy remark is a close relation.

clue.text: Simple life form frantic to keep functioning

indicators.note: to keep means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: mad means frantic or frenzied
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A primitive organism desperate to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Old biological term for a single-celled organism; also a philosophical unit of being.

clue.text: Wanderer is less wet having got paper for absorption

indicators.note: absorption means being soaked up, so one word is taken into the other

parts.note: drier, comparative of dry
FT, the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A tramp gets less damp after acquiring some blotting paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests blotting paper but is the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who roams aimlessly from place to place without settling.

clue.text: One of our cheaper competitors of yesteryear or now?

definitions.text: One of our cheaper competitors of yesteryear
definitions.meaning: a former British tabloid that rivalled the Independent, closed in 1995

explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the Independent newspaper; its old rival was a cheaper British daily that closed in 1995.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of a defunct British daily newspaper, and an adverb meaning at the present time.

clue.text: No real rest for one never lacking drive?

definitions.text: No real rest for one never lacking drive?

parts.words: No real rest for one never lacking drive?
parts.note: a break spent doing what one does at work, as a bus driver might spend leave driving

explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' looks like ambition but means driving a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for leisure time spent doing much the same as one's usual job.

clue.text: Nervous Irish politicians at present?

indicators.note: at means placed next to, so the party follows the tense

parts.note: the present is a grammatical tense
DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Irish politicians currently feeling anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at present' looks like a phrase meaning now, but 'present' is a tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious and stiff with worry, an informal phrasal adjective.

clue.text: See about following saint's distinctive manner

indicators.note: following places the turned see after the saint
about signals the see's name is turned round

parts.note: Ely, a cathedral city and bishop's see in England

explanation.surface: Look at a saint's characteristic way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, here Ely in Cambridgeshire; 'about' turns it into YLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic way of doing, writing or dressing.
